title: Paddy overview
content: Paddy (Oryza sativa) is a cereal crop grown in Tamil Nadu. In Tamil Nadu paddy is grown in Kuruvai (June–September), Samba (August–January), Thaladi and Navarai seasons. Duration: 105 to 150 days depending on variety.

title: Paddy sowing/planting season
content: In Tamil Nadu paddy is grown in Kuruvai (June–September), Samba (August–January), Thaladi and Navarai seasons.

title: Paddy crop duration
content: Paddy takes 105 to 150 days depending on variety.

title: Soil for Paddy
content: Clay or clay-loam soils that hold water suit paddy.

title: Irrigation for Paddy
content: Critical stages are tillering to panicle initiation and flowering. Alternate wetting and drying after establishment saves water; avoid stress at flowering and drain the field about 10–15 days before harvest.

title: Fertilizer guidance for Paddy
content: Base fertilizer on a soil test (Soil Health Card). Apply well-decomposed organic manure before planting and split nitrogen into 2–3 doses. Zinc deficiency is common in delta soils; zinc sulphate is often recommended based on soil test. Exact quantities must come from TNAU recommendations via your agriculture office.

title: Seed for Paddy
content: Use certified seed or healthy planting material of a TNAU-recommended paddy variety suited to your district and season. Seed treatment with bio-agents (Trichoderma, Pseudomonas) and biofertilizers is commonly advised; get the method from the agriculture office.

title: Harvesting Paddy
content: Harvest when about 80–85% of grains in the panicle turn straw-coloured.

title: Post-harvest handling of Paddy
content: Dry grain to about 12–14% moisture before storage; store bags on pallets away from walls.

title: Common problems in Paddy
content: Diseases: Blast, Brown spot, Bacterial leaf blight, Sheath blight, Tungro, False smut. Pests: Yellow stem borer, Leaf folder, Brown planthopper, Green leafhopper, Gall midge, Earhead bug, Rats. Confirm diagnosis with the agriculture officer or KVK before treating.

title: நெல் பருவம்
content: தமிழ்நாட்டில் நெல் குறுவை (ஜூன்–செப்டம்பர்), சம்பா (ஆகஸ்ட்–ஜனவரி), தாளடி, நவரை பருவங்களில் பயிரிடப்படுகிறது.

title: நெல் பயிர் காலம்
content: நெல்: ரகத்தைப் பொறுத்து 105 முதல் 150 நாட்கள்.

title: நெல் பொதுவான பிரச்சனைகள்
content: நோய்கள்: குலை நோய், பழுப்புப் புள்ளி நோய், இலைக் கருகல் நோய், இலையுறைக் கருகல் நோய், துங்ரோ நோய், பொய்க் கரிப்பூட்டை நோய். பூச்சிகள்: தண்டு துளைப்பான், இலைச்சுருட்டுப் புழு, புகையான், பச்சைத் தத்துப்பூச்சி, ஆனைக்கொம்பன் ஈ, கதிர் நாவாய்ப்பூச்சி, எலி. சிகிச்சைக்கு முன் வேளாண் அலுவலர் அல்லது KVK-இல் உறுதி செய்யுங்கள்.

title: nel season
content: Tamil Nadu la nel Kuruvai (June–September), Samba (August–January), Thaladi, Navarai season la podalaam.

title: nel duration
content: nel: ragatha poruthu 105 la irundhu 150 naal.

title: nel common problems
content: Noigal: Blast, Brown spot, Bacterial leaf blight, Sheath blight, Tungro, False smut. Poochigal: Yellow stem borer, Leaf folder, Brown planthopper, Green leafhopper, Gall midge, Earhead bug, Rats. Treat panna munnadi agri officer illa KVK la confirm pannunga.

title: Tomato overview
content: Tomato (Solanum lycopersicum) is a vegetable crop grown in Tamil Nadu. Tomato is commonly transplanted in June–July, November–December and January–February. Duration: about 60–75 days from transplanting to first harvest.

title: Tomato sowing/planting season
content: Tomato is commonly transplanted in June–July, November–December and January–February.

title: Tomato crop duration
content: Tomato takes about 60–75 days from transplanting to first harvest.

title: Soil for Tomato
content: Well-drained loam rich in organic matter, pH about 6–7.

title: Irrigation for Tomato
content: Critical stages are flowering and fruit development. Irregular watering causes fruit cracking and blossom-end rot; drip with mulch works well.

title: Fertilizer guidance for Tomato
content: Base fertilizer on a soil test (Soil Health Card). Apply well-decomposed organic manure before planting and split nitrogen into 2–3 doses.  Exact quantities must come from TNAU recommendations via your agriculture office.

title: Seed for Tomato
content: Use certified seed or healthy planting material of a TNAU-recommended tomato variety suited to your district and season. Seed treatment with bio-agents (Trichoderma, Pseudomonas) and biofertilizers is commonly advised; get the method from the agriculture office.

title: Harvesting Tomato
content: Harvest at the breaker/turning stage for distant markets and red-ripe for local sale.

title: Post-harvest handling of Tomato
content: Grade, keep in shade and pack in ventilated crates; avoid heaping and bruising.

title: Common problems in Tomato
content: Diseases: Early blight, Late blight, Septoria leaf spot, Tomato leaf curl, Bacterial wilt, Damping off. Pests: Fruit / pod borer (Helicoverpa), Whitefly, Serpentine leaf miner, Tomato pinworm (Tuta), Mealybug. Confirm diagnosis with the agriculture officer or KVK before treating.

title: தக்காளி பருவம்
content: தக்காளி ஜூன்–ஜூலை, நவம்பர்–டிசம்பர், ஜனவரி–பிப்ரவரி மாதங்களில் நடவு செய்யப்படுகிறது.

title: தக்காளி பயிர் காலம்
content: தக்காளி: நடவு செய்த சுமார் 60–75 நாட்களில் முதல் அறுவடை.

title: தக்காளி பொதுவான பிரச்சனைகள்
content: நோய்கள்: முன் கருகல் நோய், பின் கருகல் நோய், செப்டோரியா இலைப்புள்ளி நோய், இலைச்சுருள் நோய், பாக்டீரியா வாடல் நோய், நாற்றழுகல் நோய். பூச்சிகள்: காய்ப்புழு, வெள்ளை ஈ, இலைச் சுரங்கப் புழு, டூட்டா புழு, மாவுப்பூச்சி. சிகிச்சைக்கு முன் வேளாண் அலுவலர் அல்லது KVK-இல் உறுதி செய்யுங்கள்.

title: thakkali season
content: Thakkali June–July, November–December, January–February la nadavu pannalaam.

title: thakkali duration
content: thakkali: nadavu panna 60–75 naal la first aruvadai.

title: thakkali common problems
content: Noigal: Early blight, Late blight, Septoria leaf spot, Tomato leaf curl, Bacterial wilt, Damping off. Poochigal: Fruit / pod borer (Helicoverpa), Whitefly, Serpentine leaf miner, Tomato pinworm (Tuta), Mealybug. Treat panna munnadi agri officer illa KVK la confirm pannunga.

title: Chilli overview
content: Chilli (Capsicum annuum) is a vegetable/spice crop grown in Tamil Nadu. Chilli is commonly transplanted in January–February, June–July and September–October. Duration: about 75 days from transplanting to first green chilli harvest.

title: Chilli sowing/planting season
content: Chilli is commonly transplanted in January–February, June–July and September–October.

title: Chilli crop duration
content: Chilli takes about 75 days from transplanting to first green chilli harvest.

title: Soil for Chilli
content: Well-drained loam; chilli is sensitive to waterlogging.

title: Irrigation for Chilli
content: Critical stages are flowering and fruit set. Chilli suffers from both water stress and waterlogging, so ensure good drainage.

title: Fertilizer guidance for Chilli
content: Base fertilizer on a soil test (Soil Health Card). Apply well-decomposed organic manure before planting and split nitrogen into 2–3 doses.  Exact quantities must come from TNAU recommendations via your agriculture office.

title: Seed for Chilli
content: Use certified seed or healthy planting material of a TNAU-recommended chilli variety suited to your district and season. Seed treatment with bio-agents (Trichoderma, Pseudomonas) and biofertilizers is commonly advised; get the method from the agriculture office.

title: Harvesting Chilli
content: Pick green chilli when fully grown and glossy; for dry chilli, pick fully red fruits in several rounds.

title: Post-harvest handling of Chilli
content: Dry red chilli on clean tarpaulins or drying yards to prevent mould and discolouration; store in moisture-proof bags.

title: Common problems in Chilli
content: Diseases: Bacterial wilt, Damping off, Leaf curl complex, Anthracnose (fruit rot and die-back), Powdery mildew. Pests: Fruit / pod borer (Helicoverpa), Whitefly, Thrips, Yellow mite, Aphids. Confirm diagnosis with the agriculture officer or KVK before treating.

title: மிளகாய் பருவம்
content: மிளகாய் ஜனவரி–பிப்ரவரி, ஜூன்–ஜூலை, செப்டம்பர்–அக்டோபர் மாதங்களில் நடவு செய்யப்படுகிறது.

title: மிளகாய் பயிர் காலம்
content: மிளகாய்: நடவு செய்த சுமார் 75 நாட்களில் பச்சை மிளகாய் அறுவடை.

title: மிளகாய் பொதுவான பிரச்சனைகள்
content: நோய்கள்: பாக்டீரியா வாடல் நோய், நாற்றழுகல் நோய், இலைச்சுருள் நோய், பழ அழுகல் மற்றும் நுனிக்கருகல் நோய், சாம்பல் நோய். பூச்சிகள்: காய்ப்புழு, வெள்ளை ஈ, இலைப்பேன், மஞ்சள் சிலந்தி, அசுவினி. சிகிச்சைக்கு முன் வேளாண் அலுவலர் அல்லது KVK-இல் உறுதி செய்யுங்கள்.

title: milagai season
content: Milagai January–February, June–July, September–October la nadavu pannalaam.

title: milagai duration
content: milagai: nadavu panna 75 naal la pachai milagai aruvadai.

title: milagai common problems
content: Noigal: Bacterial wilt, Damping off, Leaf curl complex, Anthracnose (fruit rot and die-back), Powdery mildew. Poochigal: Fruit / pod borer (Helicoverpa), Whitefly, Thrips, Yellow mite, Aphids. Treat panna munnadi agri officer illa KVK la confirm pannunga.

title: Banana overview
content: Banana (Musa spp.) is a fruit crop grown in Tamil Nadu. Banana is commonly planted in February–April, and with the monsoon in some districts. Duration: 11 to 14 months until bunch harvest.

title: Banana sowing/planting season
content: Banana is commonly planted in February–April, and with the monsoon in some districts.

title: Banana crop duration
content: Banana takes 11 to 14 months until bunch harvest.

title: Soil for Banana
content: Deep, fertile, well-drained loam.

title: Irrigation for Banana
content: Banana needs water throughout growth, most critically at flowering and bunch development. Drip irrigation is widely used; avoid prolonged waterlogging.

title: Fertilizer guidance for Banana
content: Base fertilizer on a soil test (Soil Health Card). Apply well-decomposed organic manure before planting and split nitrogen into 2–3 doses. Banana has a high potassium requirement. Exact quantities must come from TNAU recommendations via your agriculture office.

title: Seed for Banana
content: Use certified seed or healthy planting material of a TNAU-recommended banana variety suited to your district and season. Seed treatment with bio-agents (Trichoderma, Pseudomonas) and biofertilizers is commonly advised; get the method from the agriculture office.

title: Harvesting Banana
content: Harvest when fingers are well filled and ridges become rounded (about three-quarter maturity for distant markets).

title: Post-harvest handling of Banana
content: Handle bunches gently; do not store below about 13°C, which causes chilling injury.

title: Common problems in Banana
content: Diseases: Sigatoka leaf spot, Fusarium (Panama) wilt, Bunchy top. Pests: Rhizome weevil, Pseudostem weevil, Banana aphid. Confirm diagnosis with the agriculture officer or KVK before treating.

title: வாழை பருவம்
content: வாழை பொதுவாக பிப்ரவரி–ஏப்ரல் மாதங்களில் நடப்படுகிறது; சில மாவட்டங்களில் பருவமழை காலத்திலும் நடலாம்.

title: வாழை பயிர் காலம்
content: வாழை: தார் அறுவடைக்கு 11 முதல் 14 மாதங்கள்.

title: வாழை பொதுவான பிரச்சனைகள்
content: நோய்கள்: சிகடோகா இலைப்புள்ளி நோய், பனாமா வாடல் நோய், முடிக்கொத்து நோய். பூச்சிகள்: கிழங்கு கூன்வண்டு, தண்டு கூன்வண்டு, வாழை அசுவினி. சிகிச்சைக்கு முன் வேளாண் அலுவலர் அல்லது KVK-இல் உறுதி செய்யுங்கள்.

title: vaazhai season
content: Vaazhai podhuva February–April la nadalaam; sila district la monsoon time layum nadalaam.

title: vaazhai duration
content: vaazhai: thaar aruvadaiku 11 la irundhu 14 maasam.

title: vaazhai common problems
content: Noigal: Sigatoka leaf spot, Fusarium (Panama) wilt, Bunchy top. Poochigal: Rhizome weevil, Pseudostem weevil, Banana aphid. Treat panna munnadi agri officer illa KVK la confirm pannunga.

title: Coconut overview
content: Coconut (Cocos nucifera) is a plantation crop grown in Tamil Nadu. Coconut seedlings are best planted at the start of the monsoon (June–July or September–October). Duration: about 6–7 years to bearing for tall varieties and 3–4 years for hybrid/dwarf varieties.

title: Coconut sowing/planting season
content: Coconut seedlings are best planted at the start of the monsoon (June–July or September–October).

title: Coconut crop duration
content: Coconut takes about 6–7 years to bearing for tall varieties and 3–4 years for hybrid/dwarf varieties.

title: Soil for Coconut
content: Well-drained red loam, sandy loam or coastal sandy soils.

title: Irrigation for Coconut
content: Coconut needs regular irrigation in summer; water stress reduces nut set in later harvests. Basin or drip irrigation with husk or frond mulch conserves moisture.

title: Fertilizer guidance for Coconut
content: Base fertilizer on a soil test (Soil Health Card). Apply well-decomposed organic manure before planting and split nitrogen into 2–3 doses. Manure is applied annually in basins around the palm. Exact quantities must come from TNAU recommendations via your agriculture office.

title: Seed for Coconut
content: Use certified seed or healthy planting material of a TNAU-recommended coconut variety suited to your district and season. Seed treatment with bio-agents (Trichoderma, Pseudomonas) and biofertilizers is commonly advised; get the method from the agriculture office.

title: Harvesting Coconut
content: Nuts mature about 11–12 months after the spathe opens; harvest every 45–60 days.

title: Post-harvest handling of Coconut
content: For copra, dry kernels to about 6% moisture; store nuts in a dry, ventilated place.

title: Common problems in Coconut
content: Diseases: Bud rot, Thanjavur wilt (basal stem rot), Stem bleeding. Pests: Rhinoceros beetle, Red palm weevil, Black-headed caterpillar, Eriophyid mite, Rugose spiralling whitefly, Rats. Confirm diagnosis with the agriculture officer or KVK before treating.

title: தென்னை பருவம்
content: தென்னங்கன்றுகளை பருவமழை தொடக்கத்தில் (ஜூன்–ஜூலை அல்லது செப்டம்பர்–அக்டோபர்) நடுவது நல்லது.

title: தென்னை பயிர் காலம்
content: தென்னை: நெட்டை ரகங்கள் சுமார் 6–7 ஆண்டுகளில், வீரிய/குட்டை ரகங்கள் சுமார் 3–4 ஆண்டுகளில் காய்க்கும்.

title: தென்னை பொதுவான பிரச்சனைகள்
content: நோய்கள்: குருத்தழுகல் நோய், தஞ்சாவூர் வாடல் நோய், தண்டுக் கசிவு நோய். பூச்சிகள்: காண்டாமிருக வண்டு, சிவப்பு கூன்வண்டு, கருந்தலைப் புழு, எரியோஃபைட் சிலந்தி, சுருள் வெள்ளை ஈ, எலி. சிகிச்சைக்கு முன் வேளாண் அலுவலர் அல்லது KVK-இல் உறுதி செய்யுங்கள்.

title: thennai season
content: Thennai kandru-va monsoon start la (June–July illa September–October) nadalaam.

title: thennai duration
content: thennai: nettai ragam 6–7 varusham, hybrid/kuttai ragam 3–4 varusham la kaaikkum.

title: thennai common problems
content: Noigal: Bud rot, Thanjavur wilt (basal stem rot), Stem bleeding. Poochigal: Rhinoceros beetle, Red palm weevil, Black-headed caterpillar, Eriophyid mite, Rugose spiralling whitefly, Rats. Treat panna munnadi agri officer illa KVK la confirm pannunga.

title: Sugarcane overview
content: Sugarcane (Saccharum officinarum) is a cash crop crop grown in Tamil Nadu. Sugarcane is planted in the early season (December–January), mid season (February–March) and late season (April–May). Duration: 10 to 12 months.

title: Sugarcane sowing/planting season
content: Sugarcane is planted in the early season (December–January), mid season (February–March) and late season (April–May).

title: Sugarcane crop duration
content: Sugarcane takes 10 to 12 months.

title: Soil for Sugarcane
content: Deep loam or clay-loam with good drainage.

title: Irrigation for Sugarcane
content: The formative (tillering) phase and grand growth phase are critical. Irrigation is usually reduced near harvest; confirm timing locally.

title: Fertilizer guidance for Sugarcane
content: Base fertilizer on a soil test (Soil Health Card). Apply well-decomposed organic manure before planting and split nitrogen into 2–3 doses. Sugarcane is a heavy feeder; split nitrogen application is important. Exact quantities must come from TNAU recommendations via your agriculture office.

title: Seed for Sugarcane
content: Use certified seed or healthy planting material of a TNAU-recommended sugarcane variety suited to your district and season. Seed treatment with bio-agents (Trichoderma, Pseudomonas) and biofertilizers is commonly advised; get the method from the agriculture office.

title: Harvesting Sugarcane
content: Check maturity with a hand refractometer; when top and bottom juice Brix are nearly equal the cane is mature.

title: Post-harvest handling of Sugarcane
content: Send cane to the mill within about 24 hours of cutting to avoid sugar loss.

title: Common problems in Sugarcane
content: Diseases: Red rot, Smut, Grassy shoot. Pests: Early shoot borer, Internode borer, Woolly aphid, White grub. Confirm diagnosis with the agriculture officer or KVK before treating.

title: கரும்பு பருவம்
content: கரும்பு முன்பருவம் (டிசம்பர்–ஜனவரி), நடுப்பருவம் (பிப்ரவரி–மார்ச்), பின்பருவம் (ஏப்ரல்–மே) ஆகியவற்றில் நடவு செய்யப்படுகிறது.

title: கரும்பு பயிர் காலம்
content: கரும்பு: 10 முதல் 12 மாதங்கள்.

title: கரும்பு பொதுவான பிரச்சனைகள்
content: நோய்கள்: செவ்வழுகல் நோய், கரிப்பூட்டை நோய், புல் தோகை நோய். பூச்சிகள்: இளம் குருத்துப் புழு, கணு இடைத் துளைப்பான், பஞ்சு அசுவினி, வெள்ளைப் புழு. சிகிச்சைக்கு முன் வேளாண் அலுவலர் அல்லது KVK-இல் உறுதி செய்யுங்கள்.

title: karumbu season
content: Karumbu early season (December–January), mid season (February–March), late season (April–May) la nadavu pannalaam.

title: karumbu duration
content: karumbu: 10 la irundhu 12 maasam.

title: karumbu common problems
content: Noigal: Red rot, Smut, Grassy shoot. Poochigal: Early shoot borer, Internode borer, Woolly aphid, White grub. Treat panna munnadi agri officer illa KVK la confirm pannunga.

title: Groundnut overview
content: Groundnut (Arachis hypogaea) is a oilseed crop grown in Tamil Nadu. Groundnut is sown in June–July (rainfed) and December–January (irrigated). Duration: about 100 to 110 days.

title: Groundnut sowing/planting season
content: Groundnut is sown in June–July (rainfed) and December–January (irrigated).

title: Groundnut crop duration
content: Groundnut takes about 100 to 110 days.

title: Soil for Groundnut
content: Well-drained light soils such as red sandy loam that allow easy pegging.

title: Irrigation for Groundnut
content: Critical stages are flowering, pegging and pod development; avoid excess water at pod maturity.

title: Fertilizer guidance for Groundnut
content: Base fertilizer on a soil test (Soil Health Card). Apply well-decomposed organic manure before planting and split nitrogen into 2–3 doses. Gypsum at pegging supplies calcium and sulphur for pod filling. Exact quantities must come from TNAU recommendations via your agriculture office.

title: Seed for Groundnut
content: Use certified seed or healthy planting material of a TNAU-recommended groundnut variety suited to your district and season. Seed treatment with bio-agents (Trichoderma, Pseudomonas) and biofertilizers is commonly advised; get the method from the agriculture office.

title: Harvesting Groundnut
content: Harvest when most leaves turn yellow and the inner shell of pods turns dark.

title: Post-harvest handling of Groundnut
content: Dry pods well (around 8–9% moisture) before storage to prevent aflatoxin mould.

title: Common problems in Groundnut
content: Diseases: Early and late leaf spot (tikka), Rust, Stem rot, Dry root rot. Pests: Thrips, Leaf miner, Red hairy caterpillar, White grub, Rats. Confirm diagnosis with the agriculture officer or KVK before treating.

title: நிலக்கடலை பருவம்
content: நிலக்கடலை ஜூன்–ஜூலை (மானாவாரி), டிசம்பர்–ஜனவரி (இறவை) மாதங்களில் விதைக்கப்படுகிறது.

title: நிலக்கடலை பயிர் காலம்
content: நிலக்கடலை: சுமார் 100 முதல் 110 நாட்கள்.

title: நிலக்கடலை பொதுவான பிரச்சனைகள்
content: நோய்கள்: டிக்கா இலைப்புள்ளி நோய், துரு நோய், தண்டழுகல் நோய், வேர் அழுகல் நோய். பூச்சிகள்: இலைப்பேன், சுருள் பூச்சி, சிவப்பு கம்பளிப்புழு, வெள்ளைப் புழு, எலி. சிகிச்சைக்கு முன் வேளாண் அலுவலர் அல்லது KVK-இல் உறுதி செய்யுங்கள்.

title: nilakadalai season
content: Nilakadalai June–July (maanaavaari), December–January (iravai) la vidhaikalaam.

title: nilakadalai duration
content: nilakadalai: sumaar 100 la irundhu 110 naal.

title: nilakadalai common problems
content: Noigal: Early and late leaf spot (tikka), Rust, Stem rot, Dry root rot. Poochigal: Thrips, Leaf miner, Red hairy caterpillar, White grub, Rats. Treat panna munnadi agri officer illa KVK la confirm pannunga.

title: Cotton overview
content: Cotton (Gossypium spp.) is a fibre crop grown in Tamil Nadu. Cotton is sown in August–September (winter irrigated) and February–March (summer irrigated). Duration: 150 to 180 days.

title: Cotton sowing/planting season
content: Cotton is sown in August–September (winter irrigated) and February–March (summer irrigated).

title: Cotton crop duration
content: Cotton takes 150 to 180 days.

title: Soil for Cotton
content: Deep black soils or well-drained loams.

title: Irrigation for Cotton
content: Critical stages are flowering and boll formation; avoid waterlogging.

title: Fertilizer guidance for Cotton
content: Base fertilizer on a soil test (Soil Health Card). Apply well-decomposed organic manure before planting and split nitrogen into 2–3 doses.  Exact quantities must come from TNAU recommendations via your agriculture office.

title: Seed for Cotton
content: Use certified seed or healthy planting material of a TNAU-recommended cotton variety suited to your district and season. Seed treatment with bio-agents (Trichoderma, Pseudomonas) and biofertilizers is commonly advised; get the method from the agriculture office.

title: Harvesting Cotton
content: Pick fully opened bolls in dry weather and keep kapas clean and free of trash.

title: Post-harvest handling of Cotton
content: Store kapas dry and free from contamination; do not mix grades.

title: Common problems in Cotton
content: Diseases: Dry root rot, Bacterial blight. Pests: Fruit / pod borer (Helicoverpa), Whitefly, Thrips, Aphids, Pink bollworm, Leafhopper (jassid), Mealybug. Confirm diagnosis with the agriculture officer or KVK before treating.

title: பருத்தி பருவம்
content: பருத்தி ஆகஸ்ட்–செப்டம்பர் (குளிர்கால இறவை), பிப்ரவரி–மார்ச் (கோடை இறவை) மாதங்களில் விதைக்கப்படுகிறது.

title: பருத்தி பயிர் காலம்
content: பருத்தி: 150 முதல் 180 நாட்கள்.

title: பருத்தி பொதுவான பிரச்சனைகள்
content: நோய்கள்: வேர் அழுகல் நோய், பாக்டீரியா இலைக் கருகல் நோய். பூச்சிகள்: காய்ப்புழு, வெள்ளை ஈ, இலைப்பேன், அசுவினி, இளஞ்சிவப்பு காய்ப்புழு, தத்துப்பூச்சி, மாவுப்பூச்சி. சிகிச்சைக்கு முன் வேளாண் அலுவலர் அல்லது KVK-இல் உறுதி செய்யுங்கள்.

title: paruthi season
content: Paruthi August–September (winter iravai), February–March (summer iravai) la vidhaikalaam.

title: paruthi duration
content: paruthi: 150 la irundhu 180 naal.

title: paruthi common problems
content: Noigal: Dry root rot, Bacterial blight. Poochigal: Fruit / pod borer (Helicoverpa), Whitefly, Thrips, Aphids, Pink bollworm, Leafhopper (jassid), Mealybug. Treat panna munnadi agri officer illa KVK la confirm pannunga.

title: Maize overview
content: Maize (Zea mays) is a cereal crop grown in Tamil Nadu. Maize is sown in June–July, September–October and January–February. Duration: 95 to 110 days.

title: Maize sowing/planting season
content: Maize is sown in June–July, September–October and January–February.

title: Maize crop duration
content: Maize takes 95 to 110 days.

title: Soil for Maize
content: Well-drained loam; maize does not tolerate waterlogging.

title: Irrigation for Maize
content: Tasselling and silking are the most critical stages; stress then sharply reduces grain set. Maize is sensitive to waterlogging.

title: Fertilizer guidance for Maize
content: Base fertilizer on a soil test (Soil Health Card). Apply well-decomposed organic manure before planting and split nitrogen into 2–3 doses.  Exact quantities must come from TNAU recommendations via your agriculture office.

title: Seed for Maize
content: Use certified seed or healthy planting material of a TNAU-recommended maize variety suited to your district and season. Seed treatment with bio-agents (Trichoderma, Pseudomonas) and biofertilizers is commonly advised; get the method from the agriculture office.

title: Harvesting Maize
content: Harvest when husks are dry and papery and grains are hard with a black layer at the base.

title: Post-harvest handling of Maize
content: Dry grain to about 12–13% moisture and protect from storage pests.

title: Common problems in Maize
content: Diseases: Turcicum leaf blight, Downy mildew. Pests: Fall armyworm, Spotted stem borer. Confirm diagnosis with the agriculture officer or KVK before treating.

title: மக்காச்சோளம் பருவம்
content: மக்காச்சோளம் ஜூன்–ஜூலை, செப்டம்பர்–அக்டோபர், ஜனவரி–பிப்ரவரி மாதங்களில் விதைக்கப்படுகிறது.

title: மக்காச்சோளம் பயிர் காலம்
content: மக்காச்சோளம்: 95 முதல் 110 நாட்கள்.

title: மக்காச்சோளம் பொதுவான பிரச்சனைகள்
content: நோய்கள்: இலைக் கருகல் நோய், அடிச்சாம்பல் நோய். பூச்சிகள்: படைப்புழு, தண்டு துளைப்பான். சிகிச்சைக்கு முன் வேளாண் அலுவலர் அல்லது KVK-இல் உறுதி செய்யுங்கள்.

title: makkacholam season
content: Makkacholam June–July, September–October, January–February la vidhaikalaam.

title: makkacholam duration
content: makkacholam: 95 la irundhu 110 naal.

title: makkacholam common problems
content: Noigal: Turcicum leaf blight, Downy mildew. Poochigal: Fall armyworm, Spotted stem borer. Treat panna munnadi agri officer illa KVK la confirm pannunga.

title: Brinjal overview
content: Brinjal (Solanum melongena) is a vegetable crop grown in Tamil Nadu. Brinjal is commonly transplanted in December–January and May–June. Duration: about 55–65 days from transplanting to first harvest.

title: Brinjal sowing/planting season
content: Brinjal is commonly transplanted in December–January and May–June.

title: Brinjal crop duration
content: Brinjal takes about 55–65 days from transplanting to first harvest.

title: Soil for Brinjal
content: Well-drained loam rich in organic matter.

title: Irrigation for Brinjal
content: Flowering and fruiting are critical; give regular light irrigation.

title: Fertilizer guidance for Brinjal
content: Base fertilizer on a soil test (Soil Health Card). Apply well-decomposed organic manure before planting and split nitrogen into 2–3 doses.  Exact quantities must come from TNAU recommendations via your agriculture office.

title: Seed for Brinjal
content: Use certified seed or healthy planting material of a TNAU-recommended brinjal variety suited to your district and season. Seed treatment with bio-agents (Trichoderma, Pseudomonas) and biofertilizers is commonly advised; get the method from the agriculture office.

title: Harvesting Brinjal
content: Harvest fruits when tender, glossy and full-sized, before seeds harden.

title: Post-harvest handling of Brinjal
content: Grade and market fresh; keep in shade in ventilated containers.

title: Common problems in Brinjal
content: Diseases: Bacterial wilt, Damping off, Little leaf, Phomopsis blight and fruit rot. Pests: Whitefly, Aphids, Leafhopper (jassid), Mealybug, Shoot and fruit borer, Epilachna beetle. Confirm diagnosis with the agriculture officer or KVK before treating.

title: கத்தரி பருவம்
content: கத்தரி டிசம்பர்–ஜனவரி, மே–ஜூன் மாதங்களில் நடவு செய்யப்படுகிறது.

title: கத்தரி பயிர் காலம்
content: கத்தரி: நடவு செய்த சுமார் 55–65 நாட்களில் முதல் அறுவடை.

title: கத்தரி பொதுவான பிரச்சனைகள்
content: நோய்கள்: பாக்டீரியா வாடல் நோய், நாற்றழுகல் நோய், சிற்றிலை நோய், பழ அழுகல் நோய். பூச்சிகள்: வெள்ளை ஈ, அசுவினி, தத்துப்பூச்சி, மாவுப்பூச்சி, தண்டு மற்றும் காய் துளைப்பான், எபிலாக்னா வண்டு. சிகிச்சைக்கு முன் வேளாண் அலுவலர் அல்லது KVK-இல் உறுதி செய்யுங்கள்.

title: kathiri season
content: Kathiri December–January, May–June la nadavu pannalaam.

title: kathiri duration
content: kathiri: nadavu panna 55–65 naal la first aruvadai.

title: kathiri common problems
content: Noigal: Bacterial wilt, Damping off, Little leaf, Phomopsis blight and fruit rot. Poochigal: Whitefly, Aphids, Leafhopper (jassid), Mealybug, Shoot and fruit borer, Epilachna beetle. Treat panna munnadi agri officer illa KVK la confirm pannunga.

title: Onion (small onion) overview
content: Onion (small onion) (Allium cepa var. aggregatum) is a vegetable crop grown in Tamil Nadu. Small onion is commonly planted in April–May and October–November; timing varies by district. Duration: about 60–75 days for small onion.

title: Onion (small onion) sowing/planting season
content: Small onion is commonly planted in April–May and October–November; timing varies by district.

title: Onion (small onion) crop duration
content: Onion (small onion) takes about 60–75 days for small onion.

title: Soil for Onion (small onion)
content: Loose, well-drained loam.

title: Irrigation for Onion (small onion)
content: Shallow roots need frequent light irrigation; stopping irrigation about 10 days before harvest improves storage life.

title: Fertilizer guidance for Onion (small onion)
content: Base fertilizer on a soil test (Soil Health Card). Apply well-decomposed organic manure before planting and split nitrogen into 2–3 doses.  Exact quantities must come from TNAU recommendations via your agriculture office.

title: Seed for Onion (small onion)
content: Use certified seed or healthy planting material of a TNAU-recommended onion (small onion) variety suited to your district and season. Seed treatment with bio-agents (Trichoderma, Pseudomonas) and biofertilizers is commonly advised; get the method from the agriculture office.

title: Harvesting Onion (small onion)
content: Harvest when most tops fall over and leaves begin to dry.

title: Post-harvest handling of Onion (small onion)
content: Cure bulbs in shade and store in well-ventilated structures.

title: Common problems in Onion (small onion)
content: Diseases: Purple blotch, Basal rot. Pests: Thrips. Confirm diagnosis with the agriculture officer or KVK before treating.

title: சின்ன வெங்காயம் பருவம்
content: சின்ன வெங்காயம் பொதுவாக ஏப்ரல்–மே, அக்டோபர்–நவம்பர் மாதங்களில் நடவு செய்யப்படுகிறது; மாவட்டத்தைப் பொறுத்து மாறும்.

title: சின்ன வெங்காயம் பயிர் காலம்
content: சின்ன வெங்காயம்: சின்ன வெங்காயத்திற்கு சுமார் 60–75 நாட்கள்.

title: சின்ன வெங்காயம் பொதுவான பிரச்சனைகள்
content: நோய்கள்: ஊதா கருகல் நோய், அடி அழுகல் நோய். பூச்சிகள்: இலைப்பேன். சிகிச்சைக்கு முன் வேளாண் அலுவலர் அல்லது KVK-இல் உறுதி செய்யுங்கள்.

title: vengayam season
content: Chinna vengayam podhuva April–May, October–November la nadavu pannuvaanga; district poruthu maarum.

title: vengayam duration
content: vengayam: chinna vengayam ku sumaar 60–75 naal.

title: vengayam common problems
content: Noigal: Purple blotch, Basal rot. Poochigal: Thrips. Treat panna munnadi agri officer illa KVK la confirm pannunga.

title: Drumstick (moringa) overview
content: Drumstick (moringa) (Moringa oleifera) is a vegetable tree crop grown in Tamil Nadu. Annual drumstick varieties such as PKM-1 are commonly sown in June–July. Duration: first pods in about 6 months for annual varieties.

title: Drumstick (moringa) sowing/planting season
content: Annual drumstick varieties such as PKM-1 are commonly sown in June–July.

title: Drumstick (moringa) crop duration
content: Drumstick (moringa) takes first pods in about 6 months for annual varieties.

title: Soil for Drumstick (moringa)
content: Well-drained sandy loam; tolerates poor soils but not waterlogging.

title: Irrigation for Drumstick (moringa)
content: Drumstick is drought tolerant; irrigate at flowering and pod set and avoid waterlogging.

title: Fertilizer guidance for Drumstick (moringa)
content: Base fertilizer on a soil test (Soil Health Card). Apply well-decomposed organic manure before planting and split nitrogen into 2–3 doses.  Exact quantities must come from TNAU recommendations via your agriculture office.

title: Seed for Drumstick (moringa)
content: Use certified seed or healthy planting material of a TNAU-recommended drumstick (moringa) variety suited to your district and season. Seed treatment with bio-agents (Trichoderma, Pseudomonas) and biofertilizers is commonly advised; get the method from the agriculture office.

title: Harvesting Drumstick (moringa)
content: Harvest pods while tender, before they become fibrous.

title: Post-harvest handling of Drumstick (moringa)
content: Pods are perishable; market quickly and keep cool and shaded.

title: Common problems in Drumstick (moringa)
content: Diseases: none listed. Pests: Pod fly, Hairy caterpillar. Confirm diagnosis with the agriculture officer or KVK before treating.

title: முருங்கை பருவம்
content: ஆண்டு முருங்கை ரகங்கள் (PKM-1 போன்றவை) பொதுவாக ஜூன்–ஜூலையில் விதைக்கப்படுகின்றன.

title: முருங்கை பயிர் காலம்
content: முருங்கை: ஆண்டு ரகங்களில் சுமார் 6 மாதத்தில் முதல் காய்.

title: முருங்கை பொதுவான பிரச்சனைகள்
content: நோய்கள்: —. பூச்சிகள்: காய் ஈ, கம்பளிப்புழு. சிகிச்சைக்கு முன் வேளாண் அலுவலர் அல்லது KVK-இல் உறுதி செய்யுங்கள்.

title: murungai season
content: Aandu murungai ragam (PKM-1 maadhiri) podhuva June–July la vidhaipaanga.

title: murungai duration
content: murungai: aandu ragathula sumaar 6 maasathula first kaai.

title: murungai common problems
content: Noigal: —. Poochigal: Pod fly, Hairy caterpillar. Treat panna munnadi agri officer illa KVK la confirm pannunga.

title: Turmeric overview
content: Turmeric (Curcuma longa) is a spice crop grown in Tamil Nadu. Turmeric is planted in May–June. Duration: 7 to 9 months.

title: Turmeric sowing/planting season
content: Turmeric is planted in May–June.

title: Turmeric crop duration
content: Turmeric takes 7 to 9 months.

title: Soil for Turmeric
content: Well-drained loam rich in organic matter.

title: Irrigation for Turmeric
content: Needs frequent irrigation in early growth; avoid waterlogging, which favours rhizome rot.

title: Fertilizer guidance for Turmeric
content: Base fertilizer on a soil test (Soil Health Card). Apply well-decomposed organic manure before planting and split nitrogen into 2–3 doses.  Exact quantities must come from TNAU recommendations via your agriculture office.

title: Seed for Turmeric
content: Use certified seed or healthy planting material of a TNAU-recommended turmeric variety suited to your district and season. Seed treatment with bio-agents (Trichoderma, Pseudomonas) and biofertilizers is commonly advised; get the method from the agriculture office.

title: Harvesting Turmeric
content: Harvest when leaves turn yellow and dry, usually 7–9 months after planting.

title: Post-harvest handling of Turmeric
content: Cure rhizomes by boiling, then sun-dry and polish before storage.

title: Common problems in Turmeric
content: Diseases: Rhizome rot, Leaf spot. Pests: Shoot borer. Confirm diagnosis with the agriculture officer or KVK before treating.

title: மஞ்சள் பருவம்
content: மஞ்சள் மே–ஜூன் மாதங்களில் நடவு செய்யப்படுகிறது.

title: மஞ்சள் பயிர் காலம்
content: மஞ்சள்: 7 முதல் 9 மாதங்கள்.

title: மஞ்சள் பொதுவான பிரச்சனைகள்
content: நோய்கள்: கிழங்கு அழுகல் நோய், இலைப்புள்ளி நோய். பூச்சிகள்: தண்டு துளைப்பான். சிகிச்சைக்கு முன் வேளாண் அலுவலர் அல்லது KVK-இல் உறுதி செய்யுங்கள்.

title: manjal season
content: Manjal May–June la nadavu pannalaam.

title: manjal duration
content: manjal: 7 la irundhu 9 maasam.

title: manjal common problems
content: Noigal: Rhizome rot, Leaf spot. Poochigal: Shoot borer. Treat panna munnadi agri officer illa KVK la confirm pannunga.

title: Black gram overview
content: Black gram (Vigna mungo) is a pulse crop grown in Tamil Nadu. Black gram is sown in June–July and September–October, and as a rice-fallow crop in January in the delta. Duration: 65 to 75 days.

title: Black gram sowing/planting season
content: Black gram is sown in June–July and September–October, and as a rice-fallow crop in January in the delta.

title: Black gram crop duration
content: Black gram takes 65 to 75 days.

title: Soil for Black gram
content: Well-drained loam; also grown on residual moisture in rice fallows.

title: Irrigation for Black gram
content: Critical stages are flowering and pod filling; rice-fallow crops grow on residual moisture.

title: Fertilizer guidance for Black gram
content: Base fertilizer on a soil test (Soil Health Card). Apply well-decomposed organic manure before planting and split nitrogen into 2–3 doses. Rhizobium seed inoculation reduces the need for nitrogen. Exact quantities must come from TNAU recommendations via your agriculture office.

title: Seed for Black gram
content: Use certified seed or healthy planting material of a TNAU-recommended black gram variety suited to your district and season. Seed treatment with bio-agents (Trichoderma, Pseudomonas) and biofertilizers is commonly advised; get the method from the agriculture office.

title: Harvesting Black gram
content: Harvest when most pods turn black.

title: Post-harvest handling of Black gram
content: Dry seeds well and store in airtight containers to protect from pulse beetle.

title: Common problems in Black gram

title: Green gram overview

title: Fertilizer guidance for Green gram
content: Base fertilizer on a soil test (Soil Health Card). Apply well-decomposed organic manure before planting and split nitrogen into 2–3 doses. Rhizobium seed inoculation reduces the need for nitrogen. Exact quantities must come from TNAU recommendations via your agriculture office.

title: Seed for Green gram

title: Harvesting Green gram
content: Harvest when most pods turn black or brown; 2–3 pickings may be needed.

title: Blast (paddy)
content: Blast is a fungal disease caused by Magnaporthe oryzae.

causes: Magnaporthe oryzae; favoured by High humidity, cool nights, excess nitrogen.
prevention: Use certified disease-free seed, remove infected residues, avoid excess nitrogen, and keep good spacing and drainage.
management: Remove affected parts early; bio-agents such as Trichoderma or Pseudomonas are used for some fungal diseases. Get the correct fungicide and dose from the agriculture officer or KVK.

title: Urea
content: Urea (straight nitrogen). Nutrient content: 46% N. Main nitrogen source; apply in splits to reduce losses.

title: DAP (Diammonium phosphate)
content: DAP (Diammonium phosphate) (complex). Nutrient content: 18% N, 46% P2O5. Basal source of phosphorus and some nitrogen.

title: Muriate of potash (MOP)
content: Muriate of potash (MOP) (straight potassium). Nutrient content: 60% K2O. Main potassium source.

title: Single super phosphate (SSP)
content: Single super phosphate (SSP) (straight phosphorus). Nutrient content: 16% P2O5 plus sulphur and calcium. Phosphorus source that also supplies sulphur and calcium.

title: Ammonium sulphate
content: Ammonium sulphate (straight nitrogen). Nutrient content: 20.6% N, about 24% S. Nitrogen plus sulphur.

title: NPK complex 17:17:17
content: NPK complex 17:17:17 (complex). Nutrient content: 17% N, 17% P2O5, 17% K2O. Balanced complex fertilizer.

title: Zinc sulphate (heptahydrate)
content: Zinc sulphate (heptahydrate) (micronutrient). Nutrient content: about 21% Zn. Corrects zinc deficiency, common in paddy soils.

title: Gypsum
content: Gypsum (amendment / secondary nutrient). Nutrient content: calcium and sulphur (content varies by grade). Used for groundnut pod filling and for reclaiming sodic soils.

title: Agricultural lime
content: Agricultural lime (amendment). Nutrient content: calcium carbonate. Raises pH of acidic soils.

title: Crop-specific micronutrient mixture
content: Crop-specific micronutrient mixture (micronutrient). Nutrient content: varies by crop mixture. TNAU and the agriculture department supply crop-specific mixtures.

title: Farmyard manure
content: Farmyard manure (organic manure). Nutrient content: low and variable NPK. Improves soil structure, water holding and microbial life.

title: Compost
content: Compost (organic manure). Nutrient content: low and variable NPK. Made from decomposed farm residues.

title: Vermicompost
content: Vermicompost (organic manure). Nutrient content: higher nutrient content than ordinary compost, variable. Good for nurseries and vegetables.

title: Neem cake
content: Neem cake (organic manure). Nutrient content: NPK plus natural pest-suppressing compounds. Also reduces some soil pests and nematodes.

title: Daincha (green manure)
content: Daincha (green manure) (green manure). Nutrient content: adds nitrogen and organic matter. Grown and ploughed in before paddy.

title: Sunn hemp (green manure)
content: Sunn hemp (green manure) (green manure). Nutrient content: adds nitrogen and organic matter. Fast-growing green manure crop.

title: Azospirillum
content: Azospirillum (biofertilizer). Nutrient content: nitrogen-fixing bacteria. For non-legume crops like paddy, maize and vegetables.

title: Rhizobium
content: Rhizobium (biofertilizer). Nutrient content: nitrogen-fixing bacteria. Seed inoculant for pulses and groundnut.

title: Phosphobacteria
content: Phosphobacteria (biofertilizer). Nutrient content: phosphate-solubilising bacteria. Makes soil phosphorus more available.

title: Mycorrhiza (VAM)
content: Mycorrhiza (VAM) (biofertilizer). Nutrient content: root-associated fungi. Improves phosphorus and water uptake.

title: Panchagavya
content: Panchagavya (organic growth promoter). Nutrient content: traditional cow-product preparation. Traditional growth promoter used in organic farming; scientific evidence varies.

title: Jeevamirtham
content: Jeevamirtham (natural farming input). Nutrient content: fermented microbial preparation. Used in natural farming to boost soil microbes; evidence varies.

title: Trichoderma viride / harzianum
content: Trichoderma viride / harzianum — bio-fungicide. Targets: Soil- and seed-borne fungal diseases (root rot, damping off, wilt). Use: Seed treatment, nursery and soil application with organic manure.

title: Pseudomonas fluorescens
content: Pseudomonas fluorescens — bio-control bacterium. Targets: Several fungal and bacterial diseases, e.g. paddy blast and sheath blight suppression. Use: Seed, seedling-root dip, soil or foliar use.

title: Beauveria bassiana
content: Beauveria bassiana — entomopathogenic fungus. Targets: Caterpillars and some sucking pests. Use: Foliar use in humid conditions.

title: Metarhizium anisopliae
content: Metarhizium anisopliae — entomopathogenic fungus. Targets: Rhinoceros beetle grubs in manure pits, white grubs. Use: Applied to breeding sites and soil.

title: Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt)
content: Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) — microbial insecticide. Targets: Caterpillars (e.g. leaf folder, fruit borers). Use: Acts when larvae eat treated leaves; best on young larvae.

title: Nuclear polyhedrosis virus (HaNPV / SlNPV)
content: Nuclear polyhedrosis virus (HaNPV / SlNPV) — viral bio-insecticide. Targets: Helicoverpa and Spodoptera caterpillars. Use: Species-specific; apply in the evening.

title: Trichogramma egg parasitoid cards
content: Trichogramma egg parasitoid cards — natural enemy. Targets: Eggs of borers and caterpillars. Use: Cards are stapled to leaves at intervals; avoid chemical sprays soon after release.

title: Neem seed kernel extract / neem oil
content: Neem seed kernel extract / neem oil — botanical. Targets: Sucking pests and young caterpillars (repellent and antifeedant). Use: Best used early and as a preventive.
keywords: Neem seed kernel extract / neem oil

title: Pheromone traps
content: Pheromone traps — trap. Targets: Species-specific: stem borer, fruit borer, pink bollworm, fall armyworm, rhinoceros beetle, red palm weevil. Use: For monitoring and mass trapping; replace lures as instructed.

title: Yellow sticky traps
content: Yellow sticky traps — trap. Targets: Whitefly, aphids, leaf miner adults. Use: Place slightly above crop canopy.

title: Blue sticky traps
content: Blue sticky traps — trap. Targets: Thrips. Use: Place slightly above crop canopy.

title: Light traps
content: Light traps — trap. Targets: Night-flying moths and hoppers. Use: For monitoring and community-level control.

title: Bird perches
content: Bird perches — cultural. Targets: Caterpillars (birds feed on them). Use: T-shaped perches placed in the field.

title: Chemical pesticides (all classes)
content: Chemical pesticides (all classes) — chemical. Targets: Varies by product. Use: Use only products approved for the crop and pest, on agriculture-officer/KVK advice. Always follow the label dose, protective equipment and pre-harvest interval.

title: Flood / basin irrigation
content: Water flows over the field or into basins around plants. Simple but uses the most water; level fields well.

title: Furrow irrigation
content: Water flows in furrows between ridges. Suits row crops like cotton, maize, sugarcane; skip-furrow saves water.

title: Drip irrigation
content: Water is delivered near roots through emitters. Saves water, allows fertigation; clean filters and flush laterals regularly.

title: Sprinkler irrigation
content: Water is sprayed like rain. Suits pulses, groundnut and uneven land; avoid in high wind.

title: Rain gun
content: Large sprinkler covering a wide radius. Suits sugarcane and fodder; needs good pressure.

title: Alternate wetting and drying (paddy)
content: Field is re-flooded only after standing water disappears to a set level. Saves water in paddy without yield loss when managed well; keep water at flowering.

title: Mulching
content: Covering soil with crop residue or plastic film. Reduces evaporation and weeds.

title: Farm pond
content: Pond to harvest runoff rainwater. Provides life-saving irrigation in dry spells.

title: Red soil
content: Light, well-drained, low in nitrogen and organic matter; widespread in Tamil Nadu. Suitable crops: Groundnut, millets, pulses, vegetables, coconut. Management: Add organic manure; conserve moisture.

title: Black (cotton) soil
content: Clayey, high water holding, cracks when dry. Suitable crops: Cotton, maize, pulses, chilli. Management: Avoid working when wet; ensure drainage.

title: Alluvial (delta) soil
content: Fertile river-deposited soil of the Cauvery delta. Suitable crops: Paddy, pulses (rice fallow), banana, sugarcane. Management: Maintain drainage; zinc deficiency is common.

title: Laterite soil
content: Acidic, leached soil in high-rainfall hilly areas. Suitable crops: Plantation crops, tapioca. Management: Liming and organic matter help.

title: Coastal sandy soil
content: Very light, low water holding. Suitable crops: Coconut, cashew, casuarina. Management: Frequent light irrigation and organic matter.

title: Saline soil
content: High soluble salts; white crust on surface. Suitable crops: Salt-tolerant crops and varieties. Management: Leach salts with good-quality water and improve drainage.

title: Sodic (alkaline) soil
content: High sodium, pH above about 8.5, poor structure. Suitable crops: Tolerant varieties after reclamation. Management: Gypsum application based on soil test, with drainage and organic matter.

title: Acidic soil
content: pH below about 6.5. Suitable crops: Many crops after correction. Management: Liming based on soil test.

title: Soil pH ranges
content: Below 6.5 is acidic, 6.5–7.5 neutral (ideal for most crops), above 7.5 alkaline. Suitable crops: —. Management: Test soil before correcting pH.

title: PM-KISAN
content: ₹6,000 per year in three ₹2,000 instalments by direct benefit transfer. Eligibility: Farmer families with cultivable land in their name; income-tax payers, government employees and certain professionals excluded; e-KYC mandatory. Apply: Register on pmkisan.gov.in, at an e-Sevai/CSC centre or via the agriculture department; complete e-KYC.

title: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY)
content: Crop insurance; farmer premium capped at 2% (kharif), 1.5% (rabi), 5% (commercial/horticulture). Eligibility: Farmers growing notified crops in notified areas, including tenant farmers and sharecroppers. Apply: Enrol before the seasonal cut-off via bank, cooperative, e-Sevai centre or pmfby.gov.in; report localised loss within 72 hours.

title: Kisan Credit Card (KCC)
content: Short-term crop credit at concessional interest with subvention for prompt repayment. Eligibility: Owner cultivators, tenant farmers, sharecroppers, farmer SHGs/JLGs. Apply: Apply at a commercial bank, regional rural bank or cooperative society.

title: Soil Health Card
content: Free soil test with crop-wise fertilizer recommendations. Eligibility: All farmers. Apply: Contact the block agriculture office or soil testing laboratory.

title: PM-KUSUM (solar pumps)
content: Subsidy for standalone solar pumps and solarising grid pumps; shares fixed by the state each year. Eligibility: Individual farmers, groups, FPOs and cooperatives with a water source. Apply: Apply via the TN Agricultural Engineering Department or state portal when open.

title: PM Kisan Maandhan Yojana
content: Pension of ₹3,000 per month after age 60; farmer contribution matched by the Centre. Eligibility: Small and marginal farmers aged 18–40 with up to 2 hectares. Apply: Enrol at a Common Service Centre.

title: e-NAM
content: Online trading with transparent bidding and bank payment. Eligibility: Farmers, FPOs and traders at e-NAM linked markets. Apply: Register on enam.gov.in, the app, or at a linked regulated market.

title: Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY)
content: Support for organic inputs, training and PGS certification. Eligibility: Farmers forming or joining organic clusters. Apply: Contact the block agriculture office.

title: Sub-Mission on Agricultural Mechanisation (SMAM)
content: Subsidy on farm machinery and support for custom hiring centres. Eligibility: All farmers; priority to small/marginal, women and SC/ST farmers. Apply: Apply via the Agricultural Engineering Department / agrimachinery.nic.in when open.

title: Agriculture Infrastructure Fund
content: 3% interest subvention on loans up to ₹2 crore for post-harvest infrastructure, plus credit guarantee. Eligibility: Farmers, FPOs, PACS, agri-entrepreneurs and start-ups. Apply: Apply at agriinfra.dac.gov.in and choose a lending bank.

title: Micro Irrigation Subsidy (PMKSY – Per Drop More Crop)
content: Subsidy on drip/sprinkler; in Tamil Nadu up to 100% for small/marginal and up to 75% for others within unit-cost limits. Eligibility: Farmers with a water source and land records; small/marginal certificate for the higher subsidy. Apply: Apply at the block horticulture/agriculture office or online via TNHORTNET.

title: Uzhavar Sandhai (farmers' markets)

title: Kuruvai Special Package
content: Input support (e.g. fertilizer, seeds) for Kuruvai paddy; extended to non-delta paddy farmers in 2026–27. Eligibility: Kuruvai paddy growers in areas notified for the year. Apply: Register via the block agriculture office or Uzhavan app after announcement.

title: Free electricity for agriculture
content: Free power supply for agricultural pump sets (continued in 2026–27 budget). Eligibility: Farmers with an agricultural service connection. Apply: Apply at the local TNPDCL section office; connections follow registration seniority.

title: Paddy procurement at Direct Purchase Centres
content: MSP plus state incentive (KMS 2025–26: ₹1,560/tonne Grade A, ₹1,310/tonne common), paid to bank. Eligibility: Registered paddy farmers. Apply: Register at the nearest DPC (online registration also available) and deliver on allotted date.

content: Short-term crop loans; about ₹17,000 crore planned for 2026–27; interest benefits for timely repayment (check with society). Eligibility: Farmer members of the village cooperative credit society. Apply: Apply at the village Primary Agricultural Cooperative Credit Society.

title: Certified seed distribution
content: Certified seeds of paddy, pulses, millets and oilseeds at subsidised rates; paddy seed subsidy continued from state funds in 2026–27. Eligibility: All farmers. Apply: Buy at the block Agriculture Extension Centre.
